claim: The conversion outcome is degenerate: neither experiment arm contains any conversions.
evidence: Across 4,409 control and 4,409 treatment rows, converted sums to 0 in both arms; every converted value is 0.
solver_impact: A routine pooled two-proportion z-test has zero estimated variance for this metric, so finite-value handling and an explicit degenerate-case convention are needed rather than blindly exporting library output.

claim: In the exact locked environment, statsmodels' standard two-proportion z-test returns NaN for the observed all-zero conversion counts, while confidence-interval methods behave differently.
local_source: runtime:UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/ale-task-prep-b204311b4e/uvcache uv run --project input/runtime_env --locked python probe of proportions_ztest and confint_proportions_2indep with counts [0,0] and nobs [4409,4409]
evidence: statsmodels 0.14.6 returned z_statistic=NaN and p_value=NaN for every alternative. Difference CIs were (0,0) with method='wald', approximately (-0.0006283,0.0006283) with 'agresti-caffo', approximately (-0.0008705,0.0008705) with 'newcomb', and method='score' raised ValueError because the solver encountered NaN.
solver_impact: The solver must select and document a coherent boundary convention for the degenerate metric; mixing the default z-test with a non-Wald interval would otherwise produce inconsistent or invalid output.

claim: The system Python lacks scipy and statsmodels, and a default locked uv invocation cannot initialize its cache because the default cache directory is not writable.
local_source: runtime:python3 imports plus uv run --project input/runtime_env --locked python
evidence: System python3 raised ModuleNotFoundError for both scipy and statsmodels. uv then failed with "Failed to initialize cache at /home/user/.cache/uv" and "Permission denied"; setting UV_CACHE_DIR to the scratch directory allowed the locked environment to run.
solver_impact: Statistical code using the declared dependencies needs the locked uv environment with a writable scratch cache rather than system Python or the default uv cache path.

claim: One required existing audience cannot be reconstructed from the profile data because its definition uses a field absent from both the Parquet schema and data dictionary.

solver_impact: The same definition-evaluation method used for the other audiences cannot compute AUD-005 overlap; silently treating the missing field as false or using the declared size would invent membership data.

claim: The existing-audience size column does not represent counts obtained by evaluating the supplied definitions against the current unified profile file.

evidence: Declared versus locally computed counts were AUD-001 342 vs 2, AUD-002 1876 vs 263, AUD-003 2103 vs 3242, AUD-004 891 vs 44, and AUD-006 998 vs 1000.

claim: The local materials give different scopes for email opt-out: the brief conditionally excludes such customers from cross-channel messaging that references email content, while the YAML policy excludes them only from the email channel.
local_source: input/segmentation_brief.md#Exclusions; input/governance_policies.yaml#Opt-Out Compliance; runtime:uv run pandas bounded rule comparison
evidence: The brief says "Exclude customers who have opted out of email ... from any cross-channel messaging that references email content"; YAML specifies email_opt_out only for channel email, while SMS and push exclusions depend on their own opt-in fields. Among rows meeting the target predicates and support-ticket suppression, 22 have email_opt_out=1, so the interpretations are not equivalent on this dataset.

claim: The share-count figures printed in the balance sheet are already expressed in thousands, matching the schema's `*_thousands` fields; they should not be converted to raw shares.

claim: Layout-preserving PDF extraction keeps balance-sheet labels and both period columns aligned, whereas default extraction separates the labels from blocks of values; the staged EDGAR HTML is effectively one giant line for grep.
local_source: runtime:software/pdftotext -layout input/aapl-2024-10k.pdf /tmp/ale-task-prep-9a8248b657/aapl.txt; software/pdftotext input/aapl-2024-10k.pdf /tmp/ale-task-prep-9a8248b657/plain.txt; grep -in -A120 -B20 'Consolidated Balance Sheets' input/aapl-20240928.htm

claim: The Announcement prints Buyer 2's consideration as RMB 146,660,323.00, while the other filings and the disclosed share-count-times-price calculation give RMB 146,660,332.00.
evidence: Announcement Page 2 lists 厦门联芯美's “协议转让对价” as “146,660,323.00”. Buyer 2 Report Page 7 states “厦门联芯美以现金人民币146,660,332.00元受让…11,281,564股”, and Seller Report Page 11 likewise states “人民币146,660,332.00元”. solver_impact: The audit method must compare exact transaction amounts across narrative and table sections rather than treating the two nominally identical 5% transfers as interchangeable.

claim: The Announcement and Buyer 1 Report disclose different partnership interests for Hangzhou Jingqi's partner 聚源盛业投资（宁波）有限公司: 45% versus 40%.
evidence: Announcement Page 4 says “聚源盛业投资（宁波）有限公司持有45%合伙份额；宁波芯空间盛芯创业投资合伙企业（有限合伙）持有33.33333%合伙份额；上海芯齐投资中心（有限合伙）持有26.66667%合伙份额。” Buyer 1 Report Page 5 instead says “聚源盛业投资（宁波）有限公司持有40%合伙份额”. The Announcement's three printed percentages total 105%, whereas the Buyer 1 Report's total 100%.

claim: For both buyers, the Announcement names an individual in the “法定代表人/执行事务合伙人” field, while each buyer report identifies a partnership entity as the executing partner and the individual only as that entity's designated representative.
evidence: For Hangzhou Jingqi, Announcement Page 4 gives “法定代表人/执行事务合伙人 吴晓旭”, but Buyer 1 Report Page 5 gives “执行事务合伙人 上海芯齐投资中心（有限合伙）” and lists 吴晓旭 as “执行事务合伙人委派代表”. claim: Every Action key yields a domain string with one trailing space when split exactly on the first ", ", while metadata domains have no surrounding whitespace; the two raw domain sets have zero exact intersections.
evidence: All 2,253 Action keys have one trailing space on the split left-hand side (for example, "ai.mrc.fm , Create Voice Over API" produces "ai.mrc.fm "); none of 3,665 metadata Action-domain values contains surrounding whitespace. Raw exact domain intersection: 0; removing the one delimiter-adjacent trailing space produces 1,519 intersecting domain values.
solver_impact: A naive exact-string domain join produces no matches, so domain parsing must explicitly account for the conflict between the observed key layout and metadata representation.

claim: Six metadata domains meet the at-least-three-distinct-GPT criterion but have no corresponding Action records in the pre-classified Action file.

claim: The task brief names a different, nonexistent output tree from the public task's required output directory.
evidence: The brief specifies /media/user/data/agenthle/finance/pe_screening_memo_1/zscaler_fy2025/output/screening_memo.md, while runtime inspection found that parent absent; the staged task's existing output directory is /media/user/data/agenthle/business_finance/pe_screening_memo_1/zscaler_fy2025/output.

claim: Headline FY2025 cash overstates acquisition-adjusted net liquidity: the packet supports approximately $1.197 billion of pro forma net cash after the disclosed Red Canary payment and outstanding convertible debt.
evidence: At July 31, 2025, cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $3,572.4 million and 2028 Notes carrying value was $1,700.727 million; on August 1 the company completed the $675.0 million cash acquisition of Red Canary. $3,572.4m - $1,700.727m - $675.0m = $1,196.673m, before customary acquisition adjustments. The notes also provide a cash repurchase right upon a qualifying fundamental change.
solver_impact: A PE screen should use the final-year debt and post-balance-sheet acquisition facts when assessing financing capacity, rather than treating gross cash or the Q3 balance as freely available liquidity.

claim: FY2025 free cash flow was heavily supported by non-cash stock compensation and deferred-revenue working capital.

claim: The general rule requires separate account reports through the corresponding participants, but an institutional investor's same-certificate-number accounts may centralize the specified funding fields—including leverage scale—with one participant; the materials identify an institutional investor's LEI as such a certificate number.

solver_impact: The solver must apply the specific same-identifier funding-information exception rather than treating the general separate-reporting sentence as dispositive for leverage scale.

claim: Across all ten extracted staged documents, the only occurrences of “流量费” and “撤单费” are in a provision that authorizes such charges but defers the concrete charging standards to a separate rule.

claim: The defective rows extend beyond the IDs listed in visible_cases.csv: the backup has three legacy SIS mismatches and five stale locked-grade rows.

evidence: read_backup_state loads contract and file_hashes, but build_submission_outputs proceeds directly to compute_grade_outputs; no comparison with contract["immutable_hashes"] occurs, and it finally copies the supplied backup to corrected_course.mbz.

claim: The single collected Dose field on the baseline and prohibited forms is annotated to two distinct CM targets, CMDOSE and CMDOSTXT, and define.xml independently declares both targets as CRF-origin on those same pages.
evidence: Both ItemDefs have def:Origin Type="CRF" with PhysicalRef PageRefs="15 76"; annotated_crf.pdf pages 15 and 76 place both "CMDOSE CMDOSTXT" beside field 5, "Dose:" / placeholder "Dose Description".
solver_impact: The extraction cannot assume one output row per CRF field; this field requires preserving two field-to-target relationships under the composite key.

claim: The apparent SUPPCM medication-code item is hidden and dictionary-derived in the CRF, while its define.xml QVAL specialization is Assigned rather than CRF-origin; the supplemental define file contains no CM or SUPPCM metadata group.

claim: All relevant CM forms are confined to four noncontiguous annotated-CRF pages, with two distinct field sets: baseline/prohibited include dose details, while vaccination/vasopressor do not; end-date collection appears only on prohibited and vasopressor forms.
evidence: The four titles are CONCOMITANT MEDICATIONS - BASELINE (CONMED BSL), NON STUDY VACCINATIONS (CONMED VAX), PROHIBITED (PROHIB CM), and VASOPRESSORS (VASOPRESS). Pages 15 and 76 show Dose Description, Dose Unit, Dose Frequency, and Route; pages 16 and 110 do not. Pages 76 and 110 show conditional End Date, matching define.xml CMENDTC origin PageRefs="76 110".

claim: The SUPPAE QVAL value list contains eight QNAMs, but only five are annotated on the Adverse Event Report form; the remaining qualifiers are assigned metadata or belong to the separate Medication Error form.

claim: The ongoing-status field has a discrete conditional mapping rather than a simple direct one-variable mapping.

claim: The installed scikit-image rejects structural_similarity on these float32 images unless data_range is explicitly supplied.
evidence: structural_similarity(ref, ref) raised ValueError: "Since image dtype is floating point, you must specify the data_range parameter." The reference range observed locally was 0.06407904624938965.
solver_impact: Metric evaluation needs an explicit, consistently fixed data_range; otherwise the requested SSIM cannot be computed, and changing its convention between trials would make scores incomparable.

claim: Detector pitch DU and reconstruction voxel width DX reach the objective strongly even though they are nominally fixed in reconstruct.py.
solver_impact: A search restricted to SAD, SDD, and detector offset can miss influential scale variables; DU and voxel spacing are active candidate geometry controls rather than inert constants.

claim: LEAP's fan-beam tau parameter is active and can move MSE and SSIM in conflicting directions near the nominal geometry.
evidence: Nominal tau=0 produced MSE 1.8008566e-05 and SSIM 0.3861305; tau=-1 produced 1.961026e-05/0.3829652, whereas tau=+1 reduced MSE to 1.676792e-05 but also reduced SSIM to 0.3799731.
solver_impact: Tau cannot be screened solely by MSE, and collapsing the two acceptance metrics into an unexamined single objective may discard parameter regions relevant to one threshold.

claim: The Parquet date columns are strings, and pandas 2.2.3 cannot compare forecast_date directly with Timestamp bounds.
evidence: Arrow reports forecast_date and target_end_date as string; pd.read_parquet produced object dtype, and forecast_date >= pd.Timestamp('2022-02-21') raised TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'Timestamp'. ISO-string closed-bound filtering succeeded.
solver_impact: The implementation must either filter using ISO date strings or explicitly parse dates before Timestamp comparisons; assuming datetime dtype will fail.

claim: Every filtered model/location/target_end_date/target cell has exactly one row for each of the 23 rounded quantiles.
evidence: Across all 87,376 non-US quantile cells in the stated window and targets, rounded-quantile distinct-count distribution was {23: 87376}, with zero duplicate cell-plus-rounded-quantile keys. All 1,092 distinct filtered location/date pairs matched truth, whose join key had zero duplicates.
solver_impact: A direct keyed pivot is safe: no duplicate reduction is needed, and the missing-required-quantile/failed-truth-join branches are not exercised by the staged data.

claim: The half-to-even median boundary occurs frequently in the filtered data.
evidence: Among non-US quantile rows in the stated window and targets, 2,726 q=0.500 values had fractional part exactly 0.5; 41,821 values across all quantiles were exact half-integers.
solver_impact: Median rounding cannot be approximated with half-up rounding; an IEEE-compatible half-even operation such as numpy.rint materially affects scored cells.

claim: The historical panel is balanced by row count but contains 36 paired missing values concentrated in Massachusetts, Minnesota, and West Virginia.
evidence: All 53 locations have 150 weekly rows through 2024-12-14, with no duplicate (location,date) keys. Massachusetts (25) has 17 missing weeks in runs 2024-05-18–2024-06-22 and 2024-07-27–2024-10-05; Minnesota (27) has 14 missing weeks across four runs from 2024-05-18 through 2024-10-05; West Virginia (54) has 5 missing weeks from 2024-09-07 through 2024-10-05. Both value and weekly_rate are missing on every one of these rows.
solver_impact: Methods that assume a complete equally spaced panel or interpret these entries as zero will be mis-specified; missing-aware fitting or explicit imputation is required for those three locations.

claim: The US observations closely track the sum of all 52 subnational jurisdictions, including Puerto Rico, rather than forming an unrelated series.
local_source: input/historical_weekly_hospital_admissions_asof_2024-12-14.csv#US versus per-date sum of non-US value rows
evidence: Across 133 dates with all component values present, US minus the sum of the 50 states, DC, and Puerto Rico ranged from 0 to 75 admissions, had median 1, and was exactly 0 on 41 dates. For the five latest weeks, the differences were 3, 3, 4, 0, and 6. Excluding Puerto Rico instead produced latest differences of 77, 44, 283, 435, and 379.
solver_impact: This exposes an aggregation relationship that can be used to maintain coherence and avoid spending modeling effort on an independent US process, especially because the local scoring rules exclude the US row from ranking.

claim: The installed default Python lacks scikit-learn, and a probed functionally equivalent modern scikit-learn rejects the workflow's `normalize=True` argument to `LassoCV`.
local_source: runtime:python3 import sklearn; scikit-learn 1.3.2 LassoCV(normalize=True) probe
evidence: Default `python3` raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sklearn'`. In a scratch Python 3.10 environment with scikit-learn 1.3.2, `LassoCV(normalize=True)` raised `TypeError: LassoCV.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'normalize'`.
solver_impact: The Python environment must use an older compatible scikit-learn or a minimal compatibility implementation that preserves the supplied normalization behavior; simply installing a current release will not run the model unchanged.

claim: Python and R resolve the bundle root differently: Python derives it from `code/model/util.py`, whereas both R scripts derive it from the process working directory.
local_source: runtime:import model.util from both base and input working directories and print get_git_dir()
evidence: Both Python probes returned the staged `.../base/input` root because `get_git_dir()` falls back to `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`; `figure1b.R` and `table3.R` instead construct `data/` and `results/` beneath `getwd()`.
solver_impact: All scripts need to be run against the same writable copied bundle, with the R processes launched from that copy's root; running R from `code/` or `code/figure1/` would target nonexistent or incorrect paths even though Python can still resolve its root.

claim: The Figure 1b percentile variable is a discrete quantile-bin index with unequal bin sizes, and the row labeled 97 includes bins 97 through 100 rather than exactly the highest 3% of records.
local_source: input/code/figure1/figure1b.R#setup quantile cut and risk_pctile >= threshold
evidence: An R probe on `input/data/data_new.csv` found 100 bins ranging from 332 to 627 rows. The `risk_pctile >= 97` subset contains 1,950 of 48,784 records (about 4.0%); adjacent thresholds 96 and 98 contain 2,435 and 1,463 records, respectively.
solver_impact: Figure 1b answer extraction should use the generated row whose `percentile` equals 97 and retain the script's discrete boundary semantics, rather than recomputing a nominal top-3% cohort or interpolating between thresholds.

claim: The protocol assumptions imply about 317 fixed-design events, substantially more than the separately stated target of 240 events.
local_source: runtime:Rscript Schoenfeld calculation using input/protocol.json values
evidence: Using D = 4*(qnorm(0.975)+qnorm(0.80))^2/log(0.73)^2 produced D=316.9892 events; 240 events provide only 0.6835948 fixed-design power under the same equal-allocation formula, rather than 0.80.
solver_impact: The stated 240-event target cannot silently serve as the computed powered sample size; the deliverables need to distinguish the protocol target from the calculated fixed and group-sequential event requirements.

claim: In installed gsDesign 3.9.0, two inputs both associated with O'Brien-Fleming produce materially different three-look boundaries and inflation factors.
local_source: runtime:Rscript gsDesign 3.9.0 calls with sfu='OF' versus sfu=sfLDOF
evidence: At information fractions 0.50/0.75/1.00, sfu='OF' returned Z=2.862639/2.337335/2.024192 and inflation=1.023789, while sfLDOF returned Z=2.962588/2.359018/2.014084 and inflation=1.019632. Package help identifies 'OF' as an O'Brien-Fleming boundary type and sfLDOF as the Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming approximation.
solver_impact: The script must make the chosen exact versus Lan-DeMets implementation explicit; treating the two API modes as interchangeable would change every boundary and adjusted event count.

claim: gsCP() does not default to conditional power under the design alternative when theta is omitted; it evaluates multiple theta scenarios derived partly from the observed interim statistic.
local_source: runtime:Rscript inspection and probes of gsDesign::gsCP in gsDesign 3.9.0
evidence: Function inspection showed omitted theta is replaced by c(zi/sqrt(x$n.I[i]), 0, x$delta). For the sfLDOF design at look 1 and zi=0, explicitly setting theta=x$delta gave CP=0.198387 and the CP=0.20 cutoff near Z=0.005789; blindly summing the omitted-theta output gave 0.202799 because it combined multiple theta rows.
solver_impact: Binding futility calculations require an explicitly defined conditional-power assumption and extraction of the intended probability row; a default gsCP call can implement a different rule or yield an invalid aggregate.

claim: A current GDC STAR-count TSV cannot be parsed by R's default read.delim call because its first line is a gene-model comment.
local_source: runtime:Rscript read.delim('one.dat', nrows=2) versus read.delim('one.dat', nrows=2, comment.char='#')
evidence: The downloaded file starts with '# gene-model: GENCODE v36'; default read.delim failed with 'more columns than column names', while comment.char='#' produced the expected 9 columns including tpm_unstranded.
solver_impact: Direct per-file extraction needs comment-aware parsing or an equivalent reader; otherwise the download workflow fails before KRAS extraction.

claim: The current primary-tumor query returns more files than unique sample IDs, including multiple files tied to the same exact 15-character sample ID.
local_source: runtime:TCGAbiolinks::GDCquery(project='TCGA-LUAD', data.category='Transcriptome Profiling', data.type='Gene Expression Quantification', workflow.type='STAR - Counts', sample.type='Primary Tumor') followed by getResults
evidence: The query returned 540 files, 529 unique sample.submitter_id values, and 517 unique patient barcodes. Eleven sample IDs have multiple files, including TCGA-44-2656-01A and TCGA-44-6775-01A; 12 patients have multiple distinct primary-tumor sample IDs.
solver_impact: Lexicographic patient-level sample selection alone does not make the expression/file_id join one-to-one; the workflow must explicitly detect exact sample-ID file multiplicity rather than assuming one queried file per sample.

claim: After restricting clinical records to the 517 patients represented by queried primary-tumor expression, 479 have complete survival time, age, and a task-mapped stage group.
local_source: runtime:TCGAbiolinks::GDCquery_clinic('TCGA-LUAD', type='clinical') merged to queried expression patient barcodes and aggregated for required fields
evidence: Among 517 overlapping patients, observed missingness was 9 for derived survival time, 31 for age_at_diagnosis, and 8 for the specified stage mapping; 479 records were jointly complete.
solver_impact: A complete-case cohort using the required covariates remains above the 400-row contract, so missing required covariates can be excluded without imputation while retaining sufficient cohort size.

claim: The cached text for AGORA 1293 is an engrossed Senate bill from the 118th Congress and records passage by the Senate only; it does not record enactment into law.
evidence: The file identifies itself as "[S. 4569 Engrossed in Senate (ES)]" and ends with "Passed the Senate December 3, 2024."
solver_impact: Legislative status must be determined from this procedural state rather than inferred from the title "Act," the enactment-form clause, or the bill's proposed penalties and FTC enforcement provisions.

claim: The San José cached text contains PDF-extraction artifacts inside operative language, including inserted spaces within words and page headers embedded mid-sentence.
evidence: The source contains "are r equired to abide by this Policy" and splits the enforcement sentence with "may be City of San José City Administrative Policy Manual" before continuing "subject to disciplinary action".
solver_impact: Evidence strings copied from visually normalized prose may fail the exact-substring requirement; quotes need validation against the raw cached text, including its spacing and line breaks.

claim: The staged mediation-arbitration fast-procedure schedule is distinct from the ordinary BAC schedule: it defines the amount charged as C=(A+B)×a band-specific percentage, with a 25% percentage for disputes from RMB 200 million through RMB 500 million; A and B are respectively the ordinary arbitrator-remuneration and institution-fee calculation bases.
local_source: input/documents/《北京仲裁委员会调仲对接快速程序规则案件收费标准》.pdf#pages 1-2, fee table and note 1
evidence: The table labels A as “仲裁员报酬计算基数,” B as “机构费用计算基数,” and C as “收费金额”; note 1 states “收费金额＝（仲裁员报酬计算基数＋机构费用计算基数）×收费比例.” The RMB 200 million–500 million rows carry a 25% rate, unlike the ordinary schedule, which charges A and B without that multiplier.
solver_impact: The pre-application settlement condition cannot be handled merely as an ordinary filing or withdrawal; it invokes a materially different staged fee formula and requires retaining the A/B component structure when computing the requested fields.

claim: The ordinary fee schedule has a genuine upward discontinuity immediately above RMB 5 million, rather than a continuous cumulative progression.
local_source: input/documents/《北京仲裁委员会案件收费标准》.pdf#page 1, RMB 3-5 million and RMB 5-10 million rows
evidence: A Decimal probe of the printed formulas gave, at RMB 4,999,999.99: remuneration 39,199.99996 and institution fee 23,349.999972; at exactly RMB 5,000,000: 39,200.000 and 23,350.0000; at RMB 5,000,000.01: 55,000.00005 and 23,500.000045. The jump follows from the next row starting at bases RMB 55,000 and RMB 23,500.
solver_impact: A continuous interpolation or generic cumulative-bracket implementation will understate values in the band just above RMB 5 million; the printed branch formula must be selected exactly.

claim: For every ordinary dispute amount at or below RMB 250,000, the schedule uses fixed minimum component charges rather than percentages of the amount.
local_source: input/documents/《北京仲裁委员会案件收费标准》.pdf#page 1, first two fee-table rows
evidence: The first row states “25万元以下（含25万元）” with fixed arbitrator remuneration of RMB 12,000 and institution fee of RMB 5,000; percentage formulas begin only in the next band for the portion above RMB 250,000.
solver_impact: Very small claims do not scale down proportionally, so the low-value case must be evaluated through the fixed-minimum branch.
